high shear granulation of a poorly soluble drug with βCD can result in retarded dissolution.

high shear granulation of ibu-profen and β-cy-clodextrin using water as a solvent resulted in a more compact granule with a high binding strength, whereas the isopropyl alcohol and water (1:1) mixture yielded a more suitable agglomerate for ibuprofen and beta-cyclodex-trin granulation.

the effects of high shear granulation parameters on ibuprofen granules prepared by the high shear mixer.
the effect of the HSM process variables on the granulation characteristics of ibuprofen/βCD and the effect of granulation scale-up.
the development of a novel HSM granulation process that could be successfully scaled up and used in a commercial scale.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HSM granulations with water or isopropanol as the granulating solv ent were not able to achieve a successful scale-up.
the HSM granulations with the water or isopropanol solvent were not able to achieve a successful scale-up due to different effects of the solvent mixture from 1 scale up to the other.
the solvent selection is a crucial step for the success of HSM granulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a successful HSM scale-up can be obtained if the granulation solvent is selected based on its ability to form liquid bridges between the particles and its ability to reduce the βCD binding tendency.
HSM granulation with water as the granulating solvent is not recommended, whereas isopropanol or isopropanol-water mixture is more suitable.
the MTR is a suitable tool for screening the effect of the solvents and the impeller speed in HSM granulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MTR technique is a useful tool to predict the wet mass consistency of granulation and the effect of process parameters on it.

the solvent mixture should be carefully selected and optimized for HSM granulation to achieve a suitable wet mass consistency and to avoid the formation of agglomerates that are too dense to disintegrate and dissolve.
HSM scale-up should be done carefully to avoid a change in the granulating medium, which could lead to a significant alteration in the granule characteristics.
